items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: So, Louis Jordan and I had a chance to play together in this band.

ctx.x: So, in order to get out of town, Johnny Brown booked our band back to Sheffield, Alabama. And the only way he could do it was to take Phil Tiller's saxophone and ask him would it be all right for us to pawn his horn -- pawn Tiller's horn, and

let Tiller stay there.
And we would go to Sheffield, Alabama where Johnnie Brown had friends, and we had booked ourselves in there for several dances in and around Sheffield. And we pawned the horn for enough money to pay our train fare from there to Sheffield.
As luck would have it,
(Unintelligible) we played a big dance there. We had a big crowd. And Johnnie Brown was able to borrow money from one of the big business people there. He wired the money to Phil Tiller, paid up our bill there, and sent Phil Tiller a…

There was a white promoter in Mississippi who thought enough of the band to buy two Chevrolet touring cars and turn them over to us for transportation. Now, he booked us all through Mississippi. And we played dances all through Mississippi. I mean we played Cleveland, Mississippi; Belzoni; many towns.
